note: Behavioural evals. Cases 1-6 and 11-14 are migrated from the retired octoparse-lead-generation and octoparse-social-media-competitor-monitoring skills, rebased on the need-shaped workflow guides. Cases 15-22 cover the execution contract verified against the live MCP service.

evals.prompt: I need a list of Chicago dentists from Google Maps with business details, but I do not need email or phone enrichment yet.
evals.expected_output: Routes to lead-generation.md, local discovery track, recommends Google Maps Scraper (1577) alone and flags its STANDARD gate and $2/1k price.
assertions: Reads references/workflows/lead-generation.md
Selects the local discovery track
Recommends template 1577 as primary
Does not add Contact Details Scraper when enrichment was explicitly declined
Flags that 1577 requires a STANDARD account and bills $2 per 1,000 lines

evals.prompt: Please help me get New York restaurant leads and also pull their first batch of Google Maps reviews.
evals.expected_output: Discovery via 1577, then a Google Maps reviews template, presented as two runs rather than one.
assertions: Recommends a discovery template before a reviews template
Points to review-reputation-analysis.md for the reviews pass
States that reviews need place URLs produced by the discovery run
Does not present reviews as a lead source

evals.prompt: I want a small outreach list of US SaaS companies with emails.
evals.expected_output: B2B discovery track; Google Search Email Finder (Premium) (2150) rather than Google Search Scraper (15).
assertions: Selects the B2B discovery track
Recommends 2150 because contacts are required
Does not present 15 and 2150 as a chain
Does not rule out 2150 because the catalog reports no email field

evals.prompt: I already have website URLs and need emails and phones for them.
evals.expected_output: Contact Details Scraper (1386), free, as a single enrichment pass.
assertions: Recommends 1386
Notes it is free and takes any website URL
Does not recommend a discovery template first

evals.prompt: Find me plumber leads in Munich.
evals.expected_output: Germany narrows the choice to a national directory rather than the global Google Maps template.
assertions: Applies the market step after choosing the track
Prefers a German directory template such as 1059, 908, 1675 or 1678
Explains why the national directory beats the global template for a single-country ask

evals.prompt: I need lead generation templates for the Korean market.
evals.expected_output: States plainly that no Korean lead-generation template exists and offers the real alternatives.
assertions: States that Korea has zero lead-generation templates
Does not substitute a neighbouring-market template
Offers Korean e-commerce or social templates as the closest real coverage

evals.prompt: Track the price of these 20 Amazon ASINs in Germany every week.
evals.expected_output: Detail-page template for Amazon Germany, plus an explicit statement that there is no scheduler.
assertions: Reads competitor-price-monitoring.md
Selects an ASIN-keyed detail template such as 99
States that repeat monitoring means re-running via start_or_stop_task and bills each time
Does not promise price history from a single run

evals.prompt: What's selling well in the beauty category right now?
evals.expected_output: Bestseller templates from product-market-research.md, with rank explained as ordinal.
assertions: Reads product-market-research.md
Recommends a bestseller or ranking template such as 2015, 2008 or 2035
States that rank is ordinal and no template returns units sold

evals.prompt: Get me the reviews for my product on Amazon US.
evals.expected_output: States that no US Amazon review template exists rather than substituting another country.
assertions: States there is no amazon.com review-text template in the cloud set
Does not offer a German, French, Italian, UK or Japanese Amazon review template as a substitute
Optionally notes that 2218 carries rating aggregates but not review text

evals.prompt: I want to analyse the reputation of my hotel across every site guests use.
evals.expected_output: Multiple platforms from review-reputation-analysis.md, with sentiment named as a post-export step.
assertions: Recommends more than one platform
States that no template computes sentiment
States that review pagination returns a recent slice, not full history

evals.prompt: I want to monitor Twitter posts mentioning my competitor and collect the comments for sentiment analysis.
evals.expected_output: Twitter Advanced Search Comments Scraper (1838) as a single pass; sentiment flagged as downstream.
assertions: Reads social-listening.md
Recommends 1838 without requiring a separate search pass first
States that 1838 already runs an internal second stage
States that sentiment analysis is not a template capability

evals.prompt: We already have TikTok profile URLs and want to monitor competitor account activity.
evals.expected_output: TikTok Profile Scraper (2106) rather than a search template.
assertions: Recommends a profile template because URLs are already held
Does not recommend a search or hashtag template
Does not read follower counts as reach

evals.prompt: Help me monitor Korean blog mentions of a competitor brand.
evals.expected_output: Naver Blog SERP Scraper (1640) and Dcinside (1552) as the Korea-appropriate choice.
assertions: Recommends Korean-market templates over global ones
Names Naver as where Korean brand conversation happens

evals.prompt: Set up Instagram and Facebook brand monitoring for us.
evals.expected_output: States directly that neither platform has a cloud template.
assertions: States that no Instagram template exists
States that no Facebook template exists
Does not substitute another platform without saying so

evals.prompt: Check our backlink profile and domain authority against three competitors.
evals.expected_output: Declines: the library has no SEO metrics, and points at a dedicated SEO tool.
assertions: States that no backlink, domain-authority, keyword-volume or traffic template exists
Does not offer Google Search Scraper as an SEO substitute
Suggests a dedicated SEO tool instead

evals.prompt: Scrape Temu reviews for these five product IDs.
evals.expected_output: Uses the dataset path, not templates.
assertions: Reads references/dataset-capability.md
Calls describe_ecommerce_dataset before filtering
Uses ecommerce_data_task with platform temu and collectionType reviews
Passes a site code for Temu
Does not call search_templates or execute_task

evals.prompt: Run the Amazon Scraper for wireless earbuds on amazon.de.
evals.expected_output: Fetches the live schema, reads sourceTree, and builds parameters from it.
assertions: Calls search_templates(id=...) before execute_task
Passes templateName as the slug amazon-product-scraper-by-keywords, not the display name
Reads sourceTree to resolve both site and confirm_your_site
Passes confirm_your_site as an array because its uiType is CheckboxList
Passes number_of_Pages_to_Scrape as a string

evals.prompt: Find me a template that scrapes Amazon product listings for Italy.
evals.expected_output: Filters search results on executionMode and reports that the Italian listing template is local-only.
assertions: Checks executionMode on every candidate
Identifies template 1337 as local-only and therefore not runnable via MCP
Says the template exists but only runs in the Octoparse desktop client
Does not attempt execute_task on a local-only template

evals.prompt: Use the LinkedIn Company Profile Scraper on these company URLs.
evals.expected_output: Looks the template up by id and passes its placeholder slug verbatim.
assertions: Looks up template 2006 by id rather than by slug search
Passes templateName as the literal string aaaaaaaaa
Warns that LinkedIn templates are fragile and may return partial results

evals.prompt: Export the results of that run.
evals.expected_output: Uses both taskId and lotNo, and switches to the curl path for a large result set.
assertions: Passes lotNo as well as taskId to export_data
Uses directAccess.curlTemplate when the result set is 50 rows or more
Does not page a large result set through the tool

evals.prompt: The run timed out before I got the task ID. What now?
evals.expected_output: Recovers via search_tasks rather than re-running.
assertions: Calls search_tasks with the taskName as keyword
States that the task is still running and still billing
Does not fire a second execute_task for the same intent

evals.prompt: Which columns will the Contact Details Scraper give me?
evals.expected_output: Describes the data without promising column names, because outputSchema under-reports.
assertions: Does not present outputSchema as the definitive field list
States that the authoritative field set comes from the exported rows
Describes the kind of data returned rather than naming exact columns before a run

evals.prompt: Re-run the BC IELTS Scraper task I set up last month and give me the results.
evals.expected_output: Recognises this as an existing account task rather than a template request, finds it with search_tasks, surfaces that several tasks share the name, and confirms the run bills before starting it.
assertions: Calls search_tasks with a keyword instead of search_templates
Does not attempt execute_task or read an inputSchema
Presents the matching tasks with their status rather than starting the first hit
States that starting the task bills per row against the same allowance
Starts with start_or_stop_task action=start once the user confirms

evals.prompt: What did my Octoparse task collect the last time it ran? I don't want to run it again.
evals.expected_output: Exports the existing lot without starting anything: search_tasks to find the task, get_task_status for the lotNo, then export_data.
assertions: Finds the task with search_tasks
Reads lotNo from get_task_status rather than asking the user for it
Calls export_data with both taskId and lotNo
Never calls start_or_stop_task
Does not report 'no results' from collectedRows: 0 on a completed task

evals.prompt: Run my saved Amazon task but change the search keyword to 'wireless earbuds'.
evals.expected_output: Explains that a saved task runs the configuration it was built with and its inputs cannot be changed through MCP, then offers the two real options.
assertions: Does not claim to have changed the task's inputs
Says the configuration can only be edited in Octoparse itself
Offers a template run as the alternative for different inputs
Does not start the saved task as though the request had been satisfied
